summary:
Cagayan Valley is one of the Philippines' regions. The national legal position on trans identity, identity documents, custody and entry applies here and is set out in the national record; what follows is what the sources document inside the region.

Two killings of trans women are documented in the region within a single national monitoring series. On 31 July 2024 a trans person named Cabansag was stabbed to death in Ilagan City, Isabela, after an alleged kidnapping and rape; three suspects were identified. On 23 June 2025 Kierra Apostol, 18, was found dead in a river in Cagayan province. She lived in Zone 7, Centro, Peñablanca, was an incoming first-year Business Management student at Cagayan State University's Caritan campus, and worked as a hair-and-makeup artist on the local pageant circuit. She had been reported missing days earlier; her body was found floating in the river between Amulung and Iguig on the morning of 23 June, and her mother told local media she saw visible signs of physical assault.

A criminology student at the University of Cagayan Valley, named online as 'Menco de Guzman' or 'Sherwin Kyqle', surrendered voluntarily at the Peñablanca police station. He admitted picking Kierra up on the Saturday night and denied involvement in her death. No outcome of the case appears in the sources.

LGBTQIA+ groups responded with demands for a full investigation and for justice, and renewed their call for the pending SOGIESC Equality Bill. Among those pressing the demand were the Cagayan State University-Andrew campus student organisation CSU Crystal, LGBT Pilipinas Taguig City Inc., and Bahaghari chairperson Reyna Valmores Salinas, who said the killing showed LGBTQ+ people remain unsafe.

Both killings are raw counts drawn from a monitoring project's national series. The sources give no homicide rate for Cagayan Valley, so trans-specific violence in the region cannot be compared against its background rate of violence, and the monitoring project's tally is a documented floor rather than a measured magnitude.
tangentialFactors:
The two regional cases sit inside a national 2024-2025 series compiled by a trans-murder monitoring project; Cagayan Valley accounts for two entries in that series, one in Isabela and one in Cagayan province.

Advocates used the June 2025 killing to press a national legislative demand, so the case has been absorbed into a country-level campaign for an anti-discrimination statute. No region-specific measure is reported in the sources as a result.
localsOnly:
Both documented victims were residents of the region. Kierra Apostol lived in Peñablanca, Cagayan, and studied at a regional state university campus; the 2024 killing took place in Ilagan City, Isabela. The suspect in the 2025 case was a local criminology student who surrendered to the municipal police.

Trans visibility in the region runs through the local pageant circuit and campus organisations. CSU Crystal, based at the Cagayan State University-Andrew campus, was among the groups demanding an investigation.
outOfScopeNotes:
No homicide rate for Cagayan Valley appears in the sources, so the two documented killings cannot be set against the region's background rate of violence; the monitoring project's count is a floor, not a measured rate.

The 2025 case had not reached a documented outcome. The suspect's admission that he collected Kierra Apostol and his denial of involvement are the only sourced statements about his role.

Whether any province, city or municipality in the region has a SOGIE anti-discrimination ordinance is not sourced here; the sources name no region-specific protection mechanism.
